sources.title: Blue Nile 30-Day Money Back Guarantee / Return Policy
supports: Eligible items may be returned within 30 days from shipment in original, unworn condition
Personalized, custom, engraved, resized-after-purchase, clearance, final-sale, and specified program purchases are excluded
Blue Nile requires original condition and documentation
sources.caveat: The policy does not expressly say whether third-party XRF testing preserves return eligibility. Confirm in writing for the exact ring before purchase.

sources.title: 16 CFR § 23.3 — Misrepresentation as to gold content
sources.publisher: Electronic Code of Federal Regulations / Federal Trade Commission
supports: Gold-content and karat-fineness claims must not be misrepresented
A gold alloy description uses a correct karat designation
The section's hollow-center example says hollow-center gold-alloy products should disclose the hollow center and should not be described as solid
sources.caveat: The eCFR identifies itself as authoritative but unofficial; the linked GovInfo source is the official published CFR edition. The hollow-center wording is not a blanket statement that every 14K alloy item is hollow.

sources.title: Official published CFR, 16 CFR § 23.3
supports: Official annual published edition of 16 CFR § 23.3
sources.caveat: The eCFR notes that an annual published edition may not include the most recent changes applied to the continuously updated eCFR.

sources.title: 16 CFR § 23.10 — Additional guidance for the use of quality marks
sources.publisher: Electronic Code of Federal Regulations / Federal Trade Commission
supports: Quality-mark guidance
National Stamping Act statement that a manufacturer/dealer who applies a precious-metal quality mark, or imports an article bearing one, should also apply that person's trademark or name
sources.caveat: The eCFR identifies itself as authoritative but unofficial; the linked GovInfo source is the official published CFR edition.

sources.title: CFPB: How do I dispute a charge on my credit card bill?
supports: CFPB says to contact the card company promptly and send a written billing-error notice within 60 calendar days after the charge appears on the statement to protect the stated rights
sources.caveat: This is not a guarantee of a refund or a substitute for reading the card agreement; defective-goods disputes can follow a different process.

sources.title: NIST publication: Traceability and Uncertainty in Alloy Analysis by Borate Fusion and XRF
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
supports: NIST publication documents X-ray fluorescence as an alloy-analysis method and discusses traceability/uncertainty
sources.caveat: This is a scientific alloy-analysis reference, not a consumer certificate or a jewelry-specific test guarantee.

sources.title: London Assay Office — X-ray fluorescence spectrometry analysis
sources.publisher: The Goldsmiths' Company Assay Office (professional assay office)
supports: The assay office lists XRF compositional analysis for metal alloys including gold
The office says its XRF analysis is usually non-destructive unless heavy plating has been used
sources.caveat: This is a UK assay-office service page, not a local Los Angeles service recommendation. Ask an independent local jeweler or laboratory about method, surface limitations, cost, and written results.

sources.title: LBMA Gold Price — benchmark information
sources.publisher: London Bullion Market Association / ICE Benchmark Administration
supports: LBMA says ICE Benchmark Administration independently administers the LBMA Gold Price auction platform
LBMA says uses of the benchmark for valuation/pricing and transactions require an IBA usage licence
sources.caveat: This page is linked as benchmark-method context only; this project has no live gold-price quote and does not display an LBMA price.

sources.title: NIST precious-metals conversion information
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology, Office of Weights and Measures
supports: NIST's Office of Weights and Measures publishes consumer guidance and links to a precious-metals conversion chart
sources.caveat: The calculator uses only the linked measurement conversion; no market price is sourced or implied.

sources.title: NIST Conversion Factors for Precious Metal Sales chart
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology, Office of Weights and Measures
supports: 1 troy ounce = 31.1034768 grams
NIST's nominal examples relate karat to a fraction of gold content
sources.caveat: The dollar amounts printed in the chart are examples, not current market prices. The calculator does not import them.
